rule: S_N must not be null
rationale: S_N is a mandatory join key linking to Acc_Info_dirty.S_N with one-to-one cardinality. While currently no nulls exist, this rule enforces referential integrity for future data loads.

rule: S_N must be unique across all records
rationale: S_N serves as a unique table-level identifier with 30 distinct values out of 30 records. Duplicates would violate the one-to-one relationship with Acc_Info_dirty.

rule: S_N must exist in Acc_Info_dirty.S_N
rationale: One-to-one key relationship requires every S_N in Cust_Bio_dirty to have a corresponding record in Acc_Info_dirty for valid joins.

rule: Account_No must not be null
rationale: Account_No is a mandatory business identifier for customer accounts with 0% missing values in current data.

rule: Account_No must be exactly 4 digits
rationale: Account numbers are 4-digit numeric codes ranging from 1001-1028 per evidence. Stored as int64 but intended as string.

rule: Account_No should be unique (flag duplicates for review)
rationale: Evidence shows 2 duplicate values (1001, 1010) appearing twice each. While joint accounts may be valid business logic, duplicates require explicit clarification.

rule: Name must use title case (allowing for lowercase particles: bin, binte, s/o, d/o)
rationale: 29 of 30 records use title case (e.g., 'Danish Bin Kamaruddin'). One record 'lim wei jie' uses all lowercase and one 'WANG SHI JIE' uses all uppercase, requiring standardisation.

check_params.logic: any(w[0].islower() or w.isupper() for w in str(row['Name']).split() if w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','d/o','s/o') and len(w) > 1)

rule: ID_No must follow Singapore NRIC/FIN format: one letter (S/T/F/G) + 7 digits + one uppercase letter
rationale: 93.3% of values follow this format. Violations observed: '1916569C' (missing prefix), 'F212233V' (6 digits instead of 7).

rule: ID_No must be unique
rationale: National identification numbers should uniquely identify individuals. Evidence shows one duplicate value 'F1011121T' requiring investigation.

rule: Race must be one of: Chinese, Malay, Indian
rationale: Evidence shows three semantic categories with casing variations (MALAY, malay, indian). Standardising to title case canonical values.

rule: Gender must be either Male or Female
rationale: Binary classification field with case inconsistencies (male, FEMALE). Must standardise to Title Case canonical values.

rule: Age must be parseable as an integer
rationale: Column stored as int64 but contains text representation 'Twenty-five' which cannot be parsed as numeric.

rule: Age must be between 0 and 120 inclusive
rationale: Domain constraint for human age. Current data includes invalid negative value -5.

rule: Age below 13 may be unrealistic for a service account
rationale: Evidence flags age value 4 as potentially unrealistic for consumer service accounts, requiring business clarification.

rule: Contact_No must not be null
rationale: Contact number is a required field for customer communication. Evidence shows 6.7% missing values (2 NULL records).

rule: Contact_No must be a valid Singapore phone number (8 digits, starting with 6, 8, or 9)
rationale: Singapore phone numbers are 8 digits with country code +65. Evidence shows formats +65, 65 prefix, and raw 8-digit numbers. One 7-digit value '8964359' is invalid.

rule: Contact_No must contain exactly 8 digits (excluding country code)
rationale: Specific check for the observed 7-digit anomaly '8964359'. Singapore numbers require exactly 8 digits.

rule: Email must contain exactly one @ symbol and no whitespace
rationale: 4 records (13.3%) are malformed: 'not-an-email' (missing @), 'useremail.com' (missing @), 'zx91 @example.com' (contains space), 'nabilah@@example.com' (double @).

rule: Country must be 'Singapore' (canonical form)
rationale: Evidence shows 8 variations of Singapore (SINGAPORE, singapore, S'pore, SG, Republic of Singapore, Singapura, 新加坡). All must standardise to 'Singapore'.

rule: Street_Name should not be in all capital letters
rationale: 96.7% of values use title case (e.g., 'Pandan Loop'). One value 'HOLLAND ROAD' uses all caps and requires standardisation.

rule: Postal_Code must be a 6-digit code
rationale: Singapore postal codes are 6 digits. Evidence shows variable lengths (4, 5, 6 digits: 6907, 99999, 410633). Stored as int64 but intended as string to preserve leading zeros.

rule: Name particles (Bin/s/o for Male, Binte/d/o for Female) must match Gender
rationale: Cultural naming conventions in Malay and Indian communities encode gender. Bin/s/o indicate Male; Binte/d/o indicate Female. Mismatches indicate data errors.

check_params.logic: (re.search(r'\b(bin|s/o)\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'male') or (re.search(r'\b(binte|d/o)\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'female')

rule: Name must match Full_Name in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: One-to-one key relationship requires consistency between Cust_Bio_dirty.Name and Acc_Info_dirty.Full_Name (accounting for casing and completeness variations).

check_params.semantic_check: Full_Name should match Name (accounting for casing, particles, and completeness variations)

rule: ID_No must match ID in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: One-to-one key relationship requires exact match between identification numbers across tables (e.g., S8421753J vs S8421753X discrepancy observed).

rule: Account_No must match Account_No in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: Referential integrity requires Account_No to be consistent across both tables for the same S_N join key.

check_params.semantic_check: Account_No must exactly match across tables
